feature: Recordings and sounds on the Library shelf, dragged onto a track
summary: A video document's recordings and sounds now sit on the Library's Media shelf with their length in the corner, stay there after their last clip is deleted, and drag onto a track the same way a file from the Finder does.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. The Library itself is off until View > Library is ticked, which is the app's rule for every document; whether video should show it without asking is a decision card on its own task.

try.do: Open a screen recording, then tick View > Library. The Media shelf shows the recording as a tile with its length in the corner.
Drag a music file from the Finder onto the timeline, then press Delete. The Audio track is empty and the music is still on the shelf.
Drag the music tile onto the empty Audio track, one second in. Watch the dashed ghost and the line over the tracks before you let go.
Drag the recording's tile to just short of the end of V1. It snaps on so the two clips meet.
Hold Command and drag the recording's tile to three seconds on V1. It goes in and pushes everything after it along.
Double click a tile, or right-click it and choose Add at Playhead. It lands at the playhead on the picked track, or on a new track when no track is picked.

evaluate: Does a clip you deleted still being on the shelf feel like a Premiere bin, or like clutter?
Is the length in the corner of the picture readable, or do you want it on a line under the name as the mock draws it?
Are the tiles wide enough? Names like Tutorial Sample.mp4 are cut in the middle at today's width.
Should double click land on a new track when no track is picked, or overwrite on V1 at the playhead the way Premiere's Overwrite does?
rough: Differs from video.html's Library: the length is a corner badge inside the picture, not a second caption line, because every tile on the shelf is one height and the shelf is height capped. Premiere's icon view puts duration in the same corner.
Differs from video.html: tiles are 68 points wide, so longer file names are cut in the middle (Tutori...e.mp4). The mock's tiles are wider, with short names like b-roll.mov.
The Library is hidden until View > Library, while the mock keeps it in the dock for video. Filed as a decision card on its own task.
Nothing puts a file into the Library without also putting it on the timeline yet (the mock's Fill the Library step: Import, drop onto the panel, capture). Filed as its own p1 task.
A tile's drag stays inside the app: letting go of one on the Finder does nothing, so a tile can never move your source file out from under the document.
